transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of a... a weird time at work lately. I'm a mechanic, and... gosh, I'm honestly a little embarrassed to even say this out loud. I really hope you don't think badly of me, or think I'm crazy. But... I keep hearing a man's voice. 

It usually comes from the garage vents, or sometimes right from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. It's not muffled or anything, it's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He just... he keeps telling me not to trust my husband, or he tells me not to touch certain cars in the shop. 

I'm sure it's just from working too hard and being stressed, right? I really want to get it fixed so I can be a good employee again. Does that sound like the kind of thing you can help me with?
Have you used methamphetamine, cocaine, or any other stimulant recently?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I would never do anything like that. I've never touched any of those kinds of drugs. I know that would be really bad for me, and I'd never want to do something that could get me in trouble or mess up my job. I just drink a little coffee in the morning to get going, but that's it, I promise. That's good, right? I mean, I'm trying my best to take care of myself.
Have you recently had a period where you felt unusually energetic or needed much less sleep than usual?

Um... well, I guess there have been times like that, but I always thought it was just me being really dedicated to my job, you know? Like, for a few weeks at a time, I'd only sleep maybe two or three hours a night. I'd wake up way before dawn, and my mind would already be at the garage, thinking about how to fix an engine or organize my tools. 

I just felt like sleeping more would be a waste of time when I could be getting things done. I mean, it's good to be productive and want to work hard, right? I didn't think it was a bad thing... I hope that doesn't sound crazy or anything. I just really wanted to do a good job. Is that... is that okay?
During those times when you were sleeping only two or three hours a night, did you feel unusually happy or excited?

Um... well, I guess you could say I felt pretty good. Like, really good. I'd be flying high, feeling like I could fix every single car in town by myself. It was like I had all the answers, you know? I was just so happy to be getting so much done. That's a positive thing, isn't it? 

But... oh, gosh, I'm a little ashamed to admit this part. Sometimes, during those same weeks... I'd get a little snappy. Like, if my husband asked why I hadn't done the dishes, or if one of the other techs at the shop moved my socket set even an inch... I'd just blow up. I'd get so mad, feeling like everyone was just trying to hold me down or get in my way. 

I always feel terrible about it afterward, I promise. I try really hard to be nice to everyone. I just... I get so focused, and then I guess I get a little irritable. Does that make sense? I really hope you don't think I'm an angry person, because I'm usually not.
Do you hear that man's voice only during those times when you're sleeping very little and feeling unusually energized?

Um... I really wish I could say it only happened when I was overtired. That would make more sense, right? Like maybe I just needed some rest and my mind was playing tricks on me. 

But... gosh, I feel a little bad admitting this, because I really want to be doing better. Even when things calm down... like, I had a quieter few weeks recently where I was actually sleeping a lot more. I wasn't making any of those huge plans to fix up the whole shop or anything. I was really trying to just be, you know, normal and relaxed. 

But... I still heard him. That man's voice in the garage. And... well, I still believed my husband and my boss were... tracking me. I know that sounds terrible, and I really don't want to think badly of them because they are good to me! I just... it didn't go away just because I was resting and feeling calmer. Does that mean I'm doing something wrong? I'm really trying my best to ignore it and just do my work, I promise.
Has there ever been a time when you heard the voice or believed people were tracking you for at least two weeks while your mood felt completely normal?

Um, yes... I think that's exactly what happened recently. Like I was just mentioning, um, I had those quieter few weeks. It was definitely for at least two weeks, maybe a bit more, where my mood felt completely fine. I was sleeping a normal amount, and I wasn't making any of those huge plans for the shop or getting snappy. I was just... normal. 

But, um... yeah, even during that whole time when I felt calm, I still heard that man's voice in the garage. And I still couldn't shake the feeling that my husband and my boss were tracking me. I really tried to just smile and do my job, and pretend everything was okay, because I don't want to cause any trouble for them. They're such good people. 

Is it... is it helpful that I'm telling you this? I really hope I'm explaining things right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
